title: Subtraction: take away & difference
examples: What is nine take away four?
If I have ten fingers and I hide four, how many are left?
How do I find the difference between twelve and seven?

explain.say: We are learning about taking away today.
If you have five fingers and you take away three, you count what is left.
Another way to take away is counting back from a big number.
Finding the difference means seeing how many more there are.
If you have six apples and your friend has four, the difference is two.
When you are counting, remember to always count back one step at a time.

faq.q: Is subtraction the same as just counting down?
faq.a: Yes, counting down is one way to do subtraction. You are taking away a set amount.
asks: Is counting down the same as minus?
Does counting down help me subtract?

faq.q: When do I use 'how many more'?
faq.a: You use 'how many more' when you need to find the difference between two groups. You see which group has more.
asks: When do I find the difference?

faq.q: Can I only subtract with fingers?
faq.a: No, you can subtract with objects like toys or even pictures. It is about taking away a group.
asks: Do I need real things to subtract?
Can I use blocks for subtraction?

faq.q: If I count back, do I stop when I reach zero?
faq.a: Yes, if you are counting back all the way, you will stop at zero. Zero means nothing is left.
asks: When counting back, what is the last number?

faq.q: Is finding the difference always bigger than the smaller number?
faq.a: No, the difference is the amount between the two numbers. It can be smaller than either number.
asks: What is the difference between 10 and 8?

facts: Subtraction means taking away a number from another number.
Counting back is a way to show subtraction.
The difference is the amount by which two numbers are apart.

quiz.say: If you have 7 balloons and 3 float away, how many are left?
quiz.why: You take 3 away from 7, so 4 are left.

wrong.0: You added the numbers together instead of taking away.
wrong.1: You only wrote down the number that was taken away.
wrong.2: You only counted the first thing that was taken away.

quiz.say: What is the difference between 10 and 6?
quiz.why: You count back from 10 until you reach 6, counting 4 steps.

wrong.0: You only subtracted the last two digits.
wrong.1: You wrote down the bigger number.
wrong.3: You added the two numbers together.

quiz.say: If you have 5 red cars and 8 blue cars, what is the difference?
quiz.why: You count how many more blue cars there are than red cars.

wrong.0: You only counted the first difference.
wrong.2: You added the number of red and blue cars.
wrong.3: You only wrote down the smaller number.
